title: utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore
---



```python
utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore(root, ttl)
```

Generic TTL-aware atomic snapshot store.

Manages timestamped CSV snapshots under ``root/<kind>/`` directories.
Directories are created lazily.  All read operations respect a caller-supplied
TTL; expired snapshots are invisible to `newest_valid` and deleted by `prune`.

The store is a pure mechanism — it knows nothing about what the files
represent or when restoring them is appropriate.  Restoring is always an
explicit caller action via `restore`.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                           | Description                                                                             | Default    |
|--------|------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| root   | [Path](`pathlib.Path`)                         | Parent directory under which per-kind subdirectories are created.                       | _required_ |
| ttl    | [pd](`pandas`).[Timedelta](`pandas.Timedelta`) | Maximum age of a snapshot for it to be considered valid by `newest_valid` and `age_of`. | _required_ |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}


::: {#d6ab56bc .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from spotforecast2_safe.utils.snapshot_store import SnapshotStore

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    root = Path(tmp)
    store = SnapshotStore(root=root, ttl=pd.Timedelta(hours=72))
    now = pd.Timestamp("2026-06-11 04:00:00", tz="UTC")

    source = root / "source.csv"
    source.write_text("x,y\n1,2\n")

    snap = store.write("mydata", source, now)
    print("snapshot path:", snap)

    valid = store.newest_valid("mydata", now)
    print("newest valid:", valid)

    dest = root / "restored.csv"
    store.restore(valid, dest)
    print("restored content:", dest.read_text())

    n = store.prune(now + pd.Timedelta(hours=73))
    print("pruned:", n)
```

### age_of { #spotforecast2_safe.utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore.age_of }

```python
utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore.age_of(snapshot, now)
```

Return the age of ``snapshot`` relative to ``now``.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type                                           | Description                                     | Default    |
|----------|------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|------------|
| snapshot | [Path](`pathlib.Path`)                         | Snapshot file whose stem encodes the timestamp. | _required_ |
| now      | [pd](`pandas`).[Timestamp](`pandas.Timestamp`) | Reference time.                                 | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                   | Description                                                     |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [pd](`pandas`).[Timedelta](`pandas.Timedelta`) \| None | ``now - snapshot_ts``, or ``None`` when the timestamp cannot be |
|        | [pd](`pandas`).[Timedelta](`pandas.Timedelta`) \| None | parsed.                                                         |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> from spotforecast2_safe.utils.snapshot_store import SnapshotStore
>>> store = SnapshotStore(root=Path("/tmp"), ttl=pd.Timedelta(hours=24))
>>> now = pd.Timestamp("2026-06-11 04:00:00", tz="UTC")
>>> snap = Path("20260610T040000Z.csv")
>>> store.age_of(snap, now)
Timedelta('1 days 00:00:00')
```

### newest_valid { #spotforecast2_safe.utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore.newest_valid }

```python
utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore.newest_valid(kind, now)
```

Return the newest valid snapshot for ``kind``, or ``None``.

A snapshot is *valid* when its filename-encoded timestamp is parseable
and within ``ttl`` of ``now``.  Files ending in ``.tmp`` and files whose
stem cannot be parsed are silently skipped (with a WARNING for the
latter).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                           | Description                       | Default    |
|--------|------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|------------|
| kind   | [str](`str`)                                   | Logical category name.            | _required_ |
| now    | [pd](`pandas`).[Timestamp](`pandas.Timestamp`) | Reference time for the TTL check. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                                                    |
|--------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [Path](`pathlib.Path`) \| None | Path of the newest valid snapshot, or ``None`` if none exists. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> from spotforecast2_safe.utils.snapshot_store import SnapshotStore
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
...     store = SnapshotStore(root=Path(tmp), ttl=pd.Timedelta(hours=24))
...     src = Path(tmp) / "d.csv"; src.write_text("x\n1\n")
...     now = pd.Timestamp("2026-06-11 04:00:00", tz="UTC")
...     _ = store.write("demo", src, now)
...     result = store.newest_valid("demo", now)
...     result is not None
True
```

### prune { #spotforecast2_safe.utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore.prune }

```python
utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore.prune(now)
```

Delete expired snapshots and stale ``.tmp`` files under ``root``.

Walks every kind subdirectory under ``root`` and removes:

* ``.csv`` snapshots whose filename-encoded timestamp is older than
  ``now - ttl``.
* Any ``.tmp`` files (left by interrupted writes).

Unparseable filenames are logged as WARNING and skipped.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                           | Description                             | Default    |
|--------|------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|------------|
| now    | [pd](`pandas`).[Timestamp](`pandas.Timestamp`) | Reference time for the age calculation. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                                                    |
|--------|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [int](`int`) | Number of files deleted (expired .csv snapshots plus any stale |
|        | [int](`int`) | .tmp files).                                                   |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> import tempfile
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> from spotforecast2_safe.utils.snapshot_store import SnapshotStore
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
...     store = SnapshotStore(root=Path(tmp), ttl=pd.Timedelta(hours=24))
...     src = Path(tmp) / "d.csv"; src.write_text("x\n1\n")
...     old_ts = pd.Timestamp("2026-06-09 04:00:00", tz="UTC")
...     now = pd.Timestamp("2026-06-11 04:00:00", tz="UTC")
...     _ = store.write("demo", src, old_ts)
...     store.prune(now)
1
```

### restore { #spotforecast2_safe.utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore.restore }

```python
utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore.restore(snapshot, dest)
```

Copy ``snapshot`` to ``dest`` atomically.

Creates parent directories as needed.  The copy is atomic at the
filesystem level: the file is written to a ``.tmp`` sibling in
``dest``'s directory, then renamed into place via ``os.replace``.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type                   | Description               | Default    |
|----------|------------------------|---------------------------|------------|
| snapshot | [Path](`pathlib.Path`) | Snapshot file to restore. | _required_ |
| dest     | [Path](`pathlib.Path`) | Destination path.         | _required_ |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> import tempfile
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> from spotforecast2_safe.utils.snapshot_store import SnapshotStore
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
...     store = SnapshotStore(root=Path(tmp), ttl=pd.Timedelta(hours=24))
...     snap = Path(tmp) / "snap.csv"; snap.write_text("a\n1\n")
...     dest = Path(tmp) / "sub" / "out.csv"
...     store.restore(snap, dest)
...     dest.read_text()
'a\n1\n'
```

### seed_from_file { #spotforecast2_safe.utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore.seed_from_file }

```python
utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore.seed_from_file(kind, source, now)
```

Bootstrap: snapshot ``source`` using its mtime if no newer snapshot exists.

Seeds the snapshot store from a pre-existing file.  Useful on the first
run after the store is introduced so that history already on disk is
preserved.  The seeded snapshot is stamped with the file's mtime (UTC),
not with ``now``.

Conditions for seeding (all must hold):

* ``source`` exists.
* The file's mtime converted to UTC is within ``ttl`` of ``now``.
* No existing snapshot for ``kind`` has a timestamp >= the file's mtime.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                           | Description                       | Default    |
|--------|------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|------------|
| kind   | [str](`str`)                                   | Logical category name.            | _required_ |
| source | [Path](`pathlib.Path`)                         | File to seed from.                | _required_ |
| now    | [pd](`pandas`).[Timestamp](`pandas.Timestamp`) | Reference time for the TTL check. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                                                       |
|--------|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [Path](`pathlib.Path`) \| None | The written snapshot path when seeding occurred, or ``None`` when |
|        | [Path](`pathlib.Path`) \| None | any condition was not met.                                        |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> from spotforecast2_safe.utils.snapshot_store import SnapshotStore
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
...     store = SnapshotStore(root=Path(tmp), ttl=pd.Timedelta(hours=72))
...     src = Path(tmp) / "src.csv"; src.write_text("v\n1\n")
...     # Back-date mtime to 10 h ago
...     now = pd.Timestamp("2026-06-11 04:00:00", tz="UTC")
...     mtime = (now - pd.Timedelta(hours=10)).timestamp()
...     os.utime(str(src), (mtime, mtime))
...     snap = store.seed_from_file("demo", src, now)
...     snap is not None
True
```

### write { #spotforecast2_safe.utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore.write }

```python
utils.snapshot_store.SnapshotStore.write(kind, source, ts)
```

Atomically copy ``source`` into the snapshot store for ``kind``.

Writes to a ``.tmp`` file in the destination directory, then replaces
the final target via ``os.replace``.  A crash between the two steps
leaves any pre-existing snapshot intact; the ``.tmp`` is ignored by
all read operations.

Timestamps are formatted as ``%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ`` (second precision).
Sub-second components of ``ts`` are silently truncated.  Two calls for
the same ``kind`` within the same UTC second produce the same filename;
the second call overwrites the first (last-writer-wins via
``os.replace``).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                           | Description                                                    | Default    |
|--------|------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| kind   | [str](`str`)                                   | Logical category name; controls the subdirectory used.         | _required_ |
| source | [Path](`pathlib.Path`)                         | File to snapshot.                                              | _required_ |
| ts     | [pd](`pandas`).[Timestamp](`pandas.Timestamp`) | Timestamp to embed in the snapshot filename (UTC recommended). | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                                                        |
|--------|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [Path](`pathlib.Path`) \| None | Path of the written snapshot file, or ``None`` (with a WARNING) if |
|        | [Path](`pathlib.Path`) \| None | ``source`` does not exist.                                         |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> import tempfile
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> import pandas as pd
>>> from spotforecast2_safe.utils.snapshot_store import SnapshotStore
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
...     store = SnapshotStore(root=Path(tmp), ttl=pd.Timedelta(hours=24))
...     src = Path(tmp) / "data.csv"
...     src.write_text("a,b\n1,2\n")
...     now = pd.Timestamp("2026-06-11 04:00:00", tz="UTC")
...     snap = store.write("demo", src, now)
...     snap.name
'20260611T040000Z.csv'
```
